advances: An explicit globally log-concave finite table, with exactly balanced full parity masses and zero reflected curvature, makes the canonical discounted weighted average lose a factor of order \(n\). The same loss survives in actual fiber volumes of explicit rational convex bodies. An exact upper bound for every center and cutoff, with an attaining center, shows that the maximum \(K\) instead grows exponentially relative to \(2^{-n}W\). A separate superlevel-to-\(K\) bound supplies an actual-body depth consumer, while the example also makes the total-mass-to-superlevel ratio grow linearly. These are obstructions to the specified averaging and superlevel-mass reductions, together with a positive resource inequality; they do not resolve the locked conjecture.

proof:
The midpoint hypothesis makes the center of every ordered positive same-parity endpoint pair a positive integer site. Thus every feasible curvature is finite and nonnegative, each \(\mathcal U_j\) is finite and contains zero, and \(\Delta_j(0)=0\). Replacing a cutoff \(L\) by the largest curvature at that center not exceeding \(L\) preserves its numerator and decreases its denominator. Hence the finite set of curvature values contains a maximizing cutoff. There are finitely many positive centers, so \(K\) is attained, and \(K(w)\ge\max_z w_z>0\) by the diagonal term. For the superlevel scalar, between consecutive positive weight values the superlevel set is constant and its mass \(a\) times cardinality increases with \(a\). A maximum is therefore attained at a positive weight value.

We first record the exact endpoint identity, including its normalization. The map \((j,v)\mapsto(j+v,j-v)\) bijects feasible oriented reflected pairs with ordered positive same-parity endpoint pairs, with inverse \((x,y)\mapsto((x+y)/2,(x-y)/2)\). A diagonal endpoint pair occurs once, at \(v=0\). For \(x=j+v\), \(y=j-v\), one has \(w_j e^{-\Delta_j(v)/2}=\sqrt{w_xw_y}\). Therefore

\[
\mathscr R(w)
=\sum_{\substack{x,y\in A\\x\equiv y\pmod2}}
\min(w_x,w_y)\sqrt{w_xw_y}.
\tag{6}
\]

This is precisely the cancellation identity in c382ad0f37a86dd8, here proved using only the stated midpoint hypothesis. The identity uses the discounted score; it does not replace it by a raw reflected-minimum sum when curvature is positive. The same finite layer-cake calculation gives
\(E_j(w)=\int_0^\infty \tfrac12e^{-L/2}B_j^\Delta(L)\,dL\le3K_j(w)\).
The moments of this kernel are \(1\) and \(2\), and its integral from zero is \(1\), so curvature-zero and diagonal terms are retained.

For completeness, the linear lower bound for the average follows by summing the band argument in 03f071403cdfc69f before selecting a center. In each nonempty parity class \(b\), choose a site of maximal weight \(m_b\). Mapping any positive site \(z\) of that class to its midpoint with the chosen site is injective within that class, and midpoint log-concavity gives \(\sum_{z\equiv b}\sqrt{m_bw_z}\le W\). Consequently the sites of that class with \(w_z\le4^{-(n+1)}m_b\) have total weight at most \(2^{-(n+1)}W\). Summing over at most \(2^n\) classes leaves total weight at least \(W/2\) at sites satisfying \(w_z>4^{-(n+1)}m_b\).

Partition those retained sites into the at most \(2^n(n+1)\) groups
\(\{z\equiv b:4^{-(r+1)}m_b<w_z\le4^{-r}m_b\}\), \(0\le r\le n\), and denote their masses by \(U_{b,r}\). Their total mass is at least \(W/2\); Cauchy-Schwarz gives
\(\sum_{b,r}U_{b,r}^2\ge W^2/[4(n+1)2^n]\).
Any two weights in one group have ratio at most four. For such endpoints,
\(\min(w_x,w_y)\sqrt{w_xw_y}\ge w_xw_y/2\).
Restrict (6) to ordered endpoint pairs in a common group and sum, obtaining
\(\mathscr R(w)\ge\tfrac12\sum_{b,r}U_{b,r}^2\ge W^2/[8(n+1)2^n]\).
Strict lower and weak upper band boundaries partition the retained sites without omitting weight ties. The argument uses injectivity only within one parity class at a time.

We next prove the superlevel inequality without changing the normalization of \(w\), \(W\), or \(K\). Let \(M:=\max_z w_z>0\), set \(u_z:=\log(M/w_z)\) for \(z\in A\), and, for \(s\ge0\), put
\(A_s:=\{z\in A:u_z\le s\}\) and \(N(s):=|A_s|\).
If \(j+v,j-v\in A_s\), midpoint log-concavity gives \(j\in A_s\), and
\(\Delta_j(v)=u_{j+v}+u_{j-v}-2u_j\le2(s-u_j)\).
Also \(\alpha_j(v)\ge Me^{-s}\). Thus, with
\(r_{A_s}(j):=|\{v\in\mathbb Z^n:j+v,j-v\in A_s\}|\),

\[
Me^{-s}r_{A_s}(j)
\le B_j^\Delta(2(s-u_j))
\le K(w)\bigl(1+2(s-u_j)\bigr)
\quad(j\in A_s).
\tag{7}
\]

All same-parity ordered endpoint pairs in \(A_s\) have their midpoint in \(A_s\). Hence the endpoint bijection and Cauchy-Schwarz give
\(\sum_{j\in A_s}r_{A_s}(j)=\sum_b|A_s\cap(b+2\mathbb Z^n)|^2\ge N(s)^2/2^n\).
Moreover \(\sum_{j\in A_s}(s-u_j)=\int_0^sN(t)\,dt\); the finitely many cutoff ties do not affect this integral. Summing (7) therefore yields

\[
\frac{Me^{-s}N(s)^2}{2^n}
\le K(w)\left[N(s)+2\int_0^sN(t)\,dt\right].
\tag{8}
\]

Set \(T(s):=Me^{-s}N(s)/2^n\). Multiplying (8) by \(Me^{-s}/2^n\) gives

\[
T(s)^2
\le K(w)T(s)+2K(w)e^{-s}\int_0^s e^tT(t)\,dt.
\tag{9}
\]

The finite step function \(N\) jumps only at the values \(u_z\); between jumps, \(T\) decreases exponentially, and it also decreases after the last jump. Thus \(T\) has a positive attained maximum \(T_*\), equal to \(\mathcal L(w)/2^n\) by the change of threshold \(a=Me^{-s}\). Thresholds larger than \(M\) give zero. At a maximizing \(s\), (9) and \(T(t)\le T_*\) give
\(T_*^2\le K(w)T_*+2K(w)T_*(1-e^{-s})\le3K(w)T_*\).
Division by \(T_*>0\) proves the second inequality of (1).

Accepted fact 03f071403cdfc69f proves both that actual positive fiber-volume tables satisfy the midpoint hypothesis and that one point satisfies \(h_S(p^\star)\ge K(w)/12\). Its actual volumes, total mass, cutoff definition, and closed-halfspace depth are exactly those used here. Substituting the proved superlevel inequality gives the claimed \(\mathcal L(w)/(36\cdot2^n)\) consumer at that same point, fixed before the halfspace. The zero-mass case is immediate without positive-center definitions.

We now verify the construction. At real height \(t\in[0,k]\), the \(i\)-th coordinate interval of \(P_n\) is
\([-\min(t/i,1),\,1+\min(t/i,1)]\).
Thus at every integer height \(t\in\{0,\ldots,k\}\), its integer coordinates are exactly

\[
x_i\in
\begin{cases}
\{-1,0,1,2\},&i\le t,\\
\{0,1\},&i>t.
\end{cases}
\tag{10}
\]

Outside these heights there are no lattice sites. Formula (10) follows directly from the original weak inequalities, including the equality case \(i=t\), so it describes the complete integer support. The number of sites at height \(t\) is \(4^t2^{k-t}=2^{k+t}\). Summing gives
\(|A_n|=2^k(2^{k+1}-1)=2^{n-1}(2^n-1)\).
The inequalities in (2) have integer coefficients and define a closed bounded convex set. The real point \(t=k/2\), \(x_i=1/2\) satisfies all of them strictly, so the polytope has nonempty interior.

The function \(f_n(t,\mathbf x):=2^{-t}\mathbf1_{P_n}(t,\mathbf x)\) is finite-valued and agrees with \(w_n\) at every integer point. On its convex positive support its logarithm is affine. Thus the global log-concavity inequality holds with equality when both endpoints are positive, and holds by nonnegativity if either endpoint is zero.

Each height has weight \(2^{k+t}2^{-t}=2^k\), and there are \(k+1=n\) heights, giving \(W_n=n2^k\). At a fixed height \(t\), each horizontal parity vector has exactly \(2^t\) sites: each of the first \(t\) coordinates offers two choices of each parity, and each remaining coordinate offers one. Its weight is therefore \(1\). Since \(n\) is even, there are \(n/2\) heights of each height parity. Every full parity class consequently has weight exactly \(n/2\).

For a center \(j=(s,\mathbf a)\in A_n\) and a positive reflected pair with height displacement \(h\), the endpoint heights are \(s+h\) and \(s-h\), and
\(w_{n,j+v}w_{n,j-v}=2^{-(s+h)}2^{-(s-h)}=2^{-2s}=w_{n,j}^2\).
This proves zero curvature for every feasible pair, including \(v=0\). Consequently, at every positive center, \(B_j^\Delta(L)=E_j(w_n)=\sum_{v\in\mathcal U_j}\alpha_j(v)\) for every \(L\ge0\), and \(K_j(w_n)=E_j(w_n)\), attained at \(L=0\).

To bound every center, fix \(j=(s,\mathbf a)\), and put \(r_s:=\min(s,k-s)\). The height constraints force \(|h|\le r_s\). For \(h\ge0\), count possible horizontal displacement coordinates using (10). If \(i\le s-h\), both endpoint coordinate sets are \(\{-1,0,1,2\}\). At an integer center there are at most three reflected choices, and there are exactly three when \(a_i\in\{0,1\}\). If \(s-h<i\le s+h\), the upper endpoint has four coordinate choices and the lower endpoint has the two choices \(\{0,1\}\). The lower coordinate determines the upper coordinate through their sum \(2a_i\), so there are at most two reflected choices. Both choices are feasible when \(a_i=0\) or \(1\). If \(i>s+h\), both endpoint coordinate sets are \(\{0,1\}\), and there is at most one reflected choice, attained at either binary center.

There are \(s-h\), \(2h\), and \(k-s-h\) coordinates of these respective types. The number of horizontal displacements is therefore at most \(3^{s-h}2^{2h}\), with simultaneous equality at every \(\mathbf a\in\{0,1\}^k\). All these displacements have minimum endpoint weight \(2^{-s-h}\). Negative \(h\) has the same count and weight by reversing the orientation; \(h=0\) is counted only once. Hence

\[
\begin{aligned}
E_j(w_n)
&\le\left(\frac32\right)^s
\left[1+2\sum_{h=1}^{r_s}\left(\frac23\right)^h\right]\\
&=\left(\frac32\right)^s
\left[5-4\left(\frac23\right)^{r_s}\right]
=:\Phi_s,
\end{aligned}
\tag{11}
\]

with equality at every binary horizontal center. A center outside \(A_n\) cannot have two positive reflected endpoints, since their midpoint would belong to the convex polytope \(P_n\). Thus no additional integer center can improve this bound.

Write \(q_0:=2/3\); this numerical ratio is not the parity-collision scalar of c382ad0f37a86dd8. Since \(r_s\le k-s\), (11) gives
\(\Phi_s\le(3/2)^k[5q_0^{k-s}-4q_0^{2(k-s)}]\).
For an integer \(a\ge0\), the bracket \(5q_0^a-4q_0^{2a}\) equals \(1\) at \(a=0\) and \(14/9\) at \(a=1\). For \(a\ge2\), one has \(0<q_0^a\le4/9<5/8\), and the polynomial \(5x-4x^2\) increases on \([0,5/8]\). Its value is then at most \(5(4/9)-4(4/9)^2=116/81<14/9\). At \(s=k-1=n-2\), one has \(r_s=k-s=1\), since \(k\ge3\), so equality holds in this bound. Binary horizontal centers attain (11), proving the exact \(K(w_n)\) in (3) and all stated attainment claims.

For the discounted average, apply (6). For heights \(t,s\) of the same parity, each fixed horizontal parity vector gives \(2^t2^s\) ordered endpoint pairs. There are \(2^k\) horizontal parity vectors. All these pairs have combined contribution
\(2^{k+t+s}2^{-\max(t,s)}2^{-(t+s)/2}=2^k2^{-|t-s|/2}\).
The midpoint is always a positive support point by convexity, so no pair is omitted. Write \(m:=n/2\). Each of the two height parities has \(m\) heights, and its remaining sum is

\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{a,b=0}^{m-1}2^{-|a-b|}
&=m+2\sum_{h=1}^{m-1}(m-h)2^{-h}\\
&=3m-4+2^{2-m}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{12}
\]

For the last equality, the two finite sums are
\(\sum_{h=1}^{m-1}2^{-h}=1-2^{1-m}\) and
\(\sum_{h=1}^{m-1}h2^{-h}=2-(m+1)2^{1-m}\).
Multiplying (12) by \(2^{k+1}\) gives the stated exact \(\mathscr R(w_n)\). Division by \(2^{-n}W_n^2=n^22^{n-2}\) gives (3). In particular, \(\mathscr R(w_n)/W_n\to3\), while \(W_n/2^n=n/2\).

At threshold \(a=2^{-r}\), \(0\le r\le k\), the superlevel set consists precisely of heights \(0,\ldots,r\). Its scalar value is
\(2^{-r}\sum_{t=0}^r2^{k+t}=2^k(2-2^{-r})\), which strictly increases with \(r\). Between weight thresholds the superlevel cardinality is constant, so a maximizing threshold is one of these values, as already proved. The last threshold \(r=k\) gives \(\mathcal L(w_n)=2^{k+1}-1=2^n-1\).

There is also a closed exact census of all oriented feasible reflected pairs, independent of their weights. For each horizontal parity vector, the numbers of sites with even and odd height are respectively
\((2^n-1)/3\) and \(2(2^n-1)/3\), by summing the geometric series \(1+4+\cdots+4^{m-1}\). The endpoint bijection therefore makes the full number of oriented positive reflected pairs, including zero, equal to
\(5\cdot2^{n-1}(2^n-1)^2/9\).
For illustration the exact consequences are:

| \(n\) | Integer bounding-box sites | Positive centers | Oriented positive reflected pairs | \(K(w_n)\) | \(\mathscr R(w_n)\) | \(\mathscr R(w_n)/(2^{-n}W_n^2)\) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| \(4\) | \(256\) | \(120\) | \(1000\) | \(21/4\) | \(48\) | \(3/4\) |
| \(6\) | \(6144\) | \(2016\) | \(70560\) | \(189/16\) | \(352\) | \(11/18\) |

An independent integer-arithmetic enumeration during this integration checked every point of \(\{0,\ldots,k\}\times\{-1,0,1,2\}^k\) against the original inequalities, every ordered same-parity positive endpoint pair, each midpoint's membership and zero curvature, every center's bound (11), binary-center equality, and the displayed exact scores for \(n=4,6\). It used dyadic integer weight units and BigInt arithmetic. The all-\(n\) support, census, and maximization proofs above do not rely on these finite checks.

It remains to verify the actual rational bodies and all approximation constants. Integrating the geometric series for \(2/(1-x^2)\) from \(0\) to \(1/3\) gives
\(\log2=2\sum_{\ell=0}^\infty[(2\ell+1)3^{2\ell+1}]^{-1}\).
The series is uniformly convergent on that interval, or its positive geometric remainder can be integrated directly. Thus \(a_n\) is rational, \(0<a_n<\log2<1\), and

\[
0<\epsilon_n:=\log2-a_n
\le\frac{2}{2J+1}\sum_{\ell=J}^\infty3^{-(2\ell+1)}
=\frac{3}{4(2n^2+1)3^{2n^2}}.
\tag{13}
\]

For every real \(t\in[0,k]\), \(1-a_nt/D>1-n^{-5}>0\). All constraints of (4) are affine with rational coefficients. They define a closed convex set bounded by \(P_n\) in the base and \(|y_\ell|\le1/2\) in the continuous coordinates. At \(t=k/2\), \(x_i=1/2\), \(\mathbf y=\mathbf0\), all inequalities are strict. Thus \(C_n\) is indeed a full-dimensional rational convex body in \(\mathbb R^{n+D}\). Its fibers at every base in \(P_n\), including boundary bases, are cubes of strictly positive side \(1-a_nt/D\). Outside \(P_n\) its fibers are empty. This proves the exact integer support and actual volume formula.

For \(0\le u<1\), direct integration gives
\(\log(1-u)+u=-\int_0^u r/(1-r)\,dr\), so
\(|\log(1-u)+u|\le u^2/[2(1-u)]\).
Use \(u=a_nt/D\le n^{-5}\) and \(0\le t<n\). At every \(z=(t,\mathbf x)\in A_n\),

\[
\begin{aligned}
\left|\log\frac{\widehat w_{n,z}}{w_{n,z}}\right|
&=\left|t\epsilon_n+D\bigl(\log(1-u)+u\bigr)\right|\\
&\le n\epsilon_n+\frac{1}{2n^4(1-n^{-5})}
\le\frac2{n^4}=\eta_n.
\end{aligned}
\tag{14}
\]

Here the binomial theorem gives \(3^{2n^2}\ge n^4\), so (13) implies
\(n\epsilon_n\le3/(8n^5)\le1/n^4\).
Also \(n^{-5}\le1/2\) makes the second term in (14) at most \(1/n^4\). These inequalities hold uniformly for all even \(n\ge4\).

Actual curvature is nonnegative because \(t\mapsto D\log(1-a_nt/D)\) is concave on \([0,k]\). More explicitly, if the center height is \(s\) and the displacement height is \(h\), the exact expression is

\[
\widehat\Delta_j(v)
=-D\log\left(1-\left(\frac{a_nh}{D-a_ns}\right)^2\right)
\le\frac{1}{n^4(1-2n^{-5})}
\le\frac8{n^4}=\delta_n.
\tag{15}
\]

To justify all domains and constants, positive endpoint widths make the squared fraction less than one. Also \(a_n<1\), \(s<n\), and \(|h|<n\) give
\(|a_nh/(D-a_ns)|\le n^{-5}/(1-n^{-5})\).
Using \(-\log(1-r)\le r/(1-r)\) with the squared fraction yields the first upper bound in (15), because
\((1-n^{-5})^2-n^{-10}=1-2n^{-5}>0\).
Finally \(1-2n^{-5}\ge1/2\) for \(n\ge4\), which even gives \(2/n^4\) as an upper bound. Alternatively, (14) and zero model curvature give \(\widehat\Delta_j(v)\le4\eta_n=\delta_n\) by writing curvature as twice the center log weight minus the two endpoint log weights.

The positive supports, and therefore every \(\mathcal U_j\), coincide. Formula (14) gives
\(e^{-\eta_n}\alpha_j(v)\le\widehat\alpha_j(v)\le e^{\eta_n}\alpha_j(v)\).
At every actual center and every cutoff \(L\ge0\),

\[
\frac{\widehat B_j^\Delta(L)}{1+L}
\le e^{\eta_n}\sum_{v\in\mathcal U_j}\alpha_j(v)
=e^{\eta_n}E_j(w_n)
\le e^{\eta_n}K(w_n).
\tag{16}
\]

For the reverse bound, fix an attaining model center \(j=(n-2,\mathbf b)\), \(\mathbf b\in\{0,1\}^{n-1}\). Cutoff \(\delta_n\) contains every actual positive reflected pair at that center by (15). Hence
\(\widehat B_j^\Delta(\delta_n)\ge e^{-\eta_n}E_j(w_n)=e^{-\eta_n}K(w_n)\).
Divide by \(1+\delta_n\) to prove the lower inequality in (5). In particular the upper estimate did not restrict the center or cutoff to the model maximizers.

Summing (14) gives \(e^{-\eta_n}W_n\le\widehat W_n\le e^{\eta_n}W_n\). Apply the endpoint identity (6) to both tables. In each summand, the endpoint minimum and the square root of their product each change by a factor between \(e^{-\eta_n}\) and \(e^{\eta_n}\). Therefore
\(e^{-2\eta_n}\mathscr R(w_n)\le\mathscr R(\widehat w_n)\le e^{2\eta_n}\mathscr R(w_n)\), including every diagonal term. Combining these inequalities gives

\[
\begin{aligned}
e^{-4\eta_n}\frac{\mathscr R(w_n)}{2^{-n}W_n^2}
&\le
\frac{\mathscr R(\widehat w_n)}{2^{-n}\widehat W_n^2}
\le
e^{4\eta_n}\frac{\mathscr R(w_n)}{2^{-n}W_n^2},\\
\frac{e^{-2\eta_n}}{1+\delta_n}\frac{2^nK(w_n)}{W_n}
&\le
\frac{2^nK(\widehat w_n)}{\widehat W_n}
\le
e^{2\eta_n}\frac{2^nK(w_n)}{W_n}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{17}
\]

Since \(\eta_n,\delta_n\to0\), (3) and (17) prove the actual average and maximum asymptotics. If \(b(n)>0\) and \(b(n)=o(n)\), the normalized actual average times \(b(n)\) tends to zero along even \(n\); it is eventually smaller than any fixed \(c>0\). This proves the asserted failure of that universal average estimate.

Finally, every positive fiber of \(C_n\) is a full-dimensional cube centered at \(\mathbf0\). Reflection through \(\mathbf0\) interchanges the two sides of any proper hyperplane through \(\mathbf0\); that hyperplane has zero \(D\)-dimensional volume. Each such closed halfspace therefore has exactly half the fiber volume. Every proper closed fiber halfspace containing \(\mathbf0\) contains a parallel halfspace through \(\mathbf0\), so its fiber volume is at least half. The constant map \(z\mapsto\mathbf0\) is an affine selector on precisely the positive fiber set \(A_n\), with relative fiber depth \(\beta=1/2\). All hypotheses of accepted fact bb2b5f9519ae23e8 apply with continuous dimension \(D\), actual weights \(\widehat w_{n,z}\), and actual total mass \(\widehat W_n\). It supplies \(z^\star\in A_n\) for which
\(h_{S_n}((z^\star,\mathbf0))\ge\widehat W_n/2^{n+1}\),
simultaneously for every containing closed ambient halfspace, including those whose boundary contains whole fibers. This verifies the claimed actual-depth behavior and completes the proof.
statement:
Let \(n\ge1\) and let \(w=(w_z)_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}\) be a nonzero, nonnegative, finitely supported table of finite real numbers, with positive support \(A:=\{z:w_z>0\}\) and \(W:=\sum_z w_z\). Assume same-parity midpoint log-concavity: if \(x,y\in A\) and \(x\equiv y\pmod2\) coordinatewise, then \(w_{(x+y)/2}^2\ge w_xw_y\). For \(j\in A\), use exactly the oriented, zero-inclusive definitions of accepted facts 03f071403cdfc69f and c382ad0f37a86dd8:

\[
\begin{aligned}
\alpha_j(v)&:=\min\{w_{j+v},w_{j-v}\},
&\mathcal U_j&:=\{v\in\mathbb Z^n:\alpha_j(v)>0\},\\
\Delta_j(v)&:=\log\frac{w_j^2}{w_{j+v}w_{j-v}},
&B_j^\Delta(L)&:=\sum_{\substack{v\in\mathcal U_j\\\Delta_j(v)\le L}}\alpha_j(v)
\quad(L\ge0),\\
K_j(w)&:=\max_{L\ge0}\frac{B_j^\Delta(L)}{1+L},
&K(w)&:=\max_{j\in A}K_j(w),\\
E_j(w)&:=\sum_{v\in\mathcal U_j}\alpha_j(v)e^{-\Delta_j(v)/2},
&\mathscr R(w)&:=\sum_{j\in A}w_jE_j(w).
\end{aligned}
\]

The argument \(w\) in \(E_j(w)\) only displays the table; this is precisely the discounted \(E_j\) of c382ad0f37a86dd8, with exponent \(-\Delta_j/2\). Define the superlevel scalar \(\mathcal L(w):=\max_{a>0}a\,|\{z:w_z\ge a\}|\). This explicitly renames the intake source's scalar \(\Lambda(w)\); the symbol \(\Lambda=\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d\) retains its mixed-lattice meaning from the locked problem. Every maximum in these definitions is attained. One has

\[
\mathscr R(w)\ge\frac{W^2}{8(n+1)2^n},
\qquad
K(w)\ge\frac{\mathcal L(w)}{3\cdot2^n}.
\tag{1}
\]

For an actual convex body \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d\), \(n,d\ge1\), let \(S:=C\cap\Lambda\ne\varnothing\), \(C_z:=\{y:(z,y)\in C\}\), and \(w_z:=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_z)\), with zero volume for empty or lower-dimensional fibers. Thus \(W=\mathcal H_d(S)\), and \(h_S\) is the unnormalized closed-halfspace depth in the locked problem. If \(W>0\), there is one \(p^\star\in S\), selected before every containing closed ambient halfspace, for which
\(h_S(p^\star)\ge K(w)/12\ge\mathcal L(w)/(36\cdot2^n)\).
The first inequality is the exact consumer of 03f071403cdfc69f. If \(W=0\), set \(\mathcal L(w)=0\); its stated depth consequence is automatic at any point of \(S\).

For every even integer \(n\ge4\), put \(k:=n-1\), use base coordinates \(z=(t,\mathbf x)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^k\), and define

\[
\begin{aligned}
P_n:=\{(t,\mathbf x):\;&0\le t\le k,\quad -1\le x_i\le2,\\
&-t\le i x_i\le i+t\quad(1\le i\le k)\},\\
A_n&:=P_n\cap\mathbb Z^n,\qquad
w_{n,z}:=
\begin{cases}
2^{-t},&z=(t,\mathbf x)\in A_n,\\
0,&z\notin A_n.
\end{cases}
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]

The polytope \(P_n\) is compact, full-dimensional, and rational. The table \(w_n\) has a finite-valued globally log-concave extension agreeing at every lattice point, including all zeros. Its support has exactly \(2^{n-1}(2^n-1)\) points, every full parity class has mass \(n/2\), and every positive reflected pair has curvature zero. With \(W_n:=\sum_z w_{n,z}\),

\[
\begin{aligned}
W_n&=n2^{n-1},\\
\mathscr R(w_n)&=2^{n-1}\bigl(3n-8+2^{3-n/2}\bigr),\\
\frac{\mathscr R(w_n)}{2^{-n}W_n^2}
&=\frac6n-\frac{16}{n^2}+\frac{2^{4-n/2}}{n^2}\sim\frac6n,\\
K(w_n)&=\frac{14}{9}\left(\frac32\right)^{n-1},
\qquad
\mathcal L(w_n)=2^n-1.
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
\]

The value of \(K(w_n)\) is an upper bound for every positive center and every cutoff, and is attained at cutoff zero at each center \((n-2,\mathbf b)\) with \(\mathbf b\in\{0,1\}^{n-1}\). In particular,
\(2^nK(w_n)/W_n=[28/(9n)](3/2)^{n-1}\to\infty\), while
\(W_n/\mathcal L(w_n)=n2^{n-1}/(2^n-1)\sim n/2\).
All asymptotics for this family are along even \(n\to\infty\).

There is the following approximation by actual rational convex bodies. Put \(D:=n^6\), \(J:=n^2\), and
\(a_n:=2\sum_{\ell=0}^{J-1}[(2\ell+1)3^{2\ell+1}]^{-1}\), and define

\[
C_n:=\left\{(t,\mathbf x,\mathbf y):
(t,\mathbf x)\in P_n,\quad
|y_\ell|\le\frac12\left(1-\frac{a_nt}{D}\right)
\quad(1\le\ell\le D)\right\}
\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^D.
\tag{4}
\]

Here the actual continuous dimension is \(d=D\). This is a compact, full-dimensional rational polytope, whose positive integer-fiber support is exactly \(A_n\). Its actual weights are \(\widehat w_{n,(t,\mathbf x)}=(1-a_nt/D)^D\) on \(A_n\) and zero outside. Put \(\widehat W_n:=\sum_z\widehat w_{n,z}\), \(\eta_n:=2/n^4\), and \(\delta_n:=8/n^4\). Curvatures, cutoff scores, and discounted scores with a hat use these actual weights in the same definitions above. Uniformly over every \(z\in A_n\) and every feasible reflected pair,

\[
\left|\log\frac{\widehat w_{n,z}}{w_{n,z}}\right|\le\eta_n,
\qquad
0\le\widehat\Delta_j(v)\le\delta_n,
\qquad
\frac{e^{-\eta_n}}{1+\delta_n}K(w_n)
\le K(\widehat w_n)\le e^{\eta_n}K(w_n).
\tag{5}
\]

The normalized discounted average satisfies
\(\mathscr R(\widehat w_n)/(2^{-n}\widehat W_n^2)\sim6/n\), and
\(2^nK(\widehat w_n)/\widehat W_n\sim[28/(9n)](3/2)^{n-1}\to\infty\).
Consequently, for every positive function \(b(n)=o(n)\) and every fixed \(c>0\), the proposed universal estimate
\(\mathscr R(w)\ge cW^2/[2^n b(n)]\)
fails even for actual fiber-volume tables of rational convex bodies. Thus the order \(n+1\) in the first inequality of (1) is sharp up to absolute constants. For \(S_n:=C_n\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^D)\), however, there is an actual point \((z^\star,\mathbf0)\in S_n\) such that
\(h_{S_n}((z^\star,\mathbf0))\ge\widehat W_n/2^{n+1}\).
